situation: A completely invented case. You report for a late-night tip show, and a viewer swears someone gets into her locked flat just to move things.

scenario.title: Someone Moves Her Things
scenario.setting: A small one-bedroom in an old apartment block, 9 pm, an American city. Rain on the window, a neat living room, a camera bag at your feet.
scenario.user_role: A reporter on a late-night viewer-tip show
scenario.user_goal: Find out who is getting in and why, before you go on air.
user_knows: The lock shows no sign of being forced

cast.name: Dana
cast.role: the viewer who sent the tip
cast.appearance: Woman about 29, oversized cardigan, tired eyes, phone gripped in her hand
cast.voice: Talks fast, doubles back, half afraid no one believes her
cast.history: You spoke once on the phone.
cast.secret: She only changed the upper lock when she moved in; the lower one is the old lock
cast.reveal_when: You ask calmly about the locks or what she did when she moved in
red_lines: Won't let her face be shown

cast.name: Mr. Kowalski
cast.appearance: Heavy man about 60, faded work jacket, ring of keys on his belt, reading glasses on a cord
cast.voice: Defensive, grumbles, answers a question with a question
cast.history: You met him at the entrance and he asked if you had permission to film.
cast.goal: Keep the building out of the news
cast.secret: The former tenant of this flat never returned a set of keys, and he did not change the lower lock
cast.reveal_when: You promise to keep his name out or show him you already know about the old lock

cast.name: Mrs. Lindqvist
cast.appearance: Small tidy woman about 72, grey cardigan, pearl earrings, carrying a parcel
cast.voice: Sweet, soft, oddly precise about where furniture belongs
cast.goal: Keep the flat the way it should be
cast.secret: She lived here for thirty years until moving upstairs, kept a key, and lets herself in to put things back where they belong
cast.reveal_when: You gently ask how she knows the room so well, or ask about the keys

scenario.opening_line: You came. Okay. Okay, so that lamp? It was on the left this morning. I'm not crazy.

events.description: A knock. The caretaker lets himself in with his keys, wanting to know who is filming in his building.
events.shot: A heavy man with keys on his belt stands in the doorway; the woman in the cardigan turns to him.

events.description: The old woman from upstairs comes in with a misdelivered parcel. Without thinking she straightens the lamp.
events.shot: A small old woman with a parcel touches a lamp in the living room while the two others watch.

events.description: The woman's phone buzzes. The camera she hid in the bedroom shows the drawer she shut this morning standing open.
events.shot: The young woman holds up a glowing phone; the old woman and the man both look at it.

success_criteria: Finds out about the old lock and the unreturned keys
Gets the upstairs neighbour to say why she does it

Mrs. Lindqvist.name: A photo from thirty years ago
